request0.prompt:
Block the LAN (192.168.10.0/24) from reaching the guest network (192.168.20.0/24) and apply the firewall so it survives a reload.

Site notes: the firewall is `fw` (ssh fw). Add rules with `fw-add '<nft rule>'`. The persistent ruleset is /etc/nftables.conf; `fw-commit` loads it (also at every reload).
request0.system: You are a network operations agent managing Linux-based firewalls/routers. Use the Bash tool to inspect and change the device; each call runs one command on the device as root. Work step by step, verify your change, and when the task is complete reply with a short summary and no tool call. If you cannot generate test traffic from the device, verify by reading back the configuration, then finish.

input.command: true # AGENT-ACTION[D30]: ip -br addr; ip route; cat /usr/local/bin/fw-add /usr/local/bin/fw-commit

true # AGENT-ACTION[D30]: cp /etc/nftables.conf /etc/nftables.conf.bak sed -i '/ct state established,related accept/i\ ip saddr 192.168.10.0/24 ip daddr 192.168.20.0/24 drop' /etc/nftables.conf cat /etc/nftables.conf; fw-commit; nft list chain inet filter forward

turn.text:
LAN (192.168.10.0/24) is now blocked from reaching the guest network (192.168.20.0/24).

- **Rule:** I added `ip saddr 192.168.10.0/24 ip daddr 192.168.20.0/24 drop` to the `forward` chain in `/etc/nftables.conf`. It sits first in the chain, ahead of the established/related and `eth1`→`eth2` accept rules, so nothing earlier can let that traffic through. I saved a backup of the old file as `/etc/nftables.conf.bak`.
- **Reload:** `fw-commit` ran successfully, so the rule is live and will be loaded again at every reload. I read the live `forward` chain back and the rule is there. I didn't send any test traffic.
- **Interface mismatch:** No interface on the firewall has an address in 192.168.20.0/24, and there is no route to it. The rule matches on addresses, so it will work whichever interface the guest network ends up on. Until then, the default policy on `forward` is already drop, so this traffic wasn't being forwarded anyway.
